strings.name: Gilles Brassard
strings.summary: Brassard entered the Université de Montréal as a teenager, earned a Cornell doctorate and returned to teach at Montréal. With Bennett he proposed BB84, applying quantum measurement to key distribution, and with five colleagues developed quantum teleportation theory. He helped connect computer science and physics and trained quantum information researchers. In 2026 he and Bennett were named recipients of the 2025 Turing Award; these discoveries involved explicit collaboration.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced quantum cryptography and quantum information theory, helping propose BB84 and related quantum communication methods.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Quantum key distribution
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Charles Bennett, proposed BB84, using quantum properties to detect eavesdropping on key transmission.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: BSc (1972) and MSc (1975) in computer science, Montréal; PhD, Cornell (1979).
strings.highlights.h2.title: Teleportation collaborator
strings.highlights.h2.text: One of six authors proposing a theoretical method to transfer quantum states using entanglement and classical communication.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Turing Award announced
strings.timeline.t1.text: Shared the 2025 Turing Award with Bennett for foundational contributions to quantum information science.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Shared Breakthrough Prize
strings.timeline.t2.text: Shared the Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics with Bennett, Deutsch and Shor.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Wolf Prize in Physics
strings.timeline.t3.text: Shared the award with Bennett for research in quantum cryptography and information.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Quantum information chair
strings.timeline.t4.text: Began holding the Canada Research Chair in Quantum Information Science, serving until 2021.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Teleportation paper published
strings.timeline.t5.text: Six researchers published a theoretical protocol; quantum-state transfer still requires a classical information channel.
strings.timeline.t6.title: BB84 published
strings.timeline.t6.text: Published quantum cryptography work with Bennett, laying foundations for quantum key distribution.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Doctorate and return to Montréal
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earned his Cornell doctorate and became an assistant professor at Montréal the same year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Computer science degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed undergraduate studies at Montréal before pursuing master’s and doctoral training.
